transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-05
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE); Connor Lee (Redwood SE); Dr. Priya Shah (Midtown CTO); Alex Kim (Eng Manager); Jordan Reyes (Security); Samir Patel (Product)

[00:00] Sofia: All right everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sofia from Redwood, AE on this account, and Connor our solutions engineer will do the heavier demo. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya: Doing well, thanks. Excited to see the model catalog we're evaluating open models for clinical note summarization.
[00:12] Connor: Great, great. Quick agenda: we'll breeze through the Console model catalog, show the benchmark page, and the compatibility matrix, then talk about deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private). Then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:20] Alex: Yep. We're most interested in latency <200ms p95 for single-turn summaries, cost under $0.01 per summary if possible, and PHI handling for on-prem options.
[00:30] Connor: Understood. We'll show tradeoffs usually smaller quantized models hit your latency targets but we need to validate quality.
[00:38] [00:38] Connor: (screen share) ok this is the model catalog page. You can filter by task, family, size, and we've got Redwood-verified benchmarks attached to each model card. Note: some transcription might say 'Redwood Dedicate' in places, that's just a caption bug.
[00:55] Priya: Nice, do the benchmarks run on H100? Our infra is Nvidia A100 on prem and GCP for cloud tests.
[01:03] Connor: Good question. Benchmarks show hardware column we've got results for A100 80GB, H100, and a CPU+int8 path. In the UI you can click 'View benchmark details' to see tokens/sec, p50/p95 latencies, and cost-per-1k-tokens based on our cost model.
[01:25] Jordan: When you say cost model, is that hosted pricing or hypothetical? We need to see dedicated pricing for reserved capacity.
[01:33] Sofia: We'll send the pricing sheet. The Console shows normalized cost numbers for quick compare; dedicated contracts get different unit rates which we'll include in the quote.
[01:42] [02:00] Connor: Here is a model card for 'open-llm-med-13b' it's fp16 natively, but we also show int8/4-bit quantized variants with bench numbers. See the compatibility matrix tab it maps model variants to supported runtimes and kernel optimizations (e.g., Triton, cuBLAS, CUTLASS).
[02:18] Priya: Do you support KV cache warm start across quantized variants? We store patient conversation history and don't want cold starts.
[02:26] Connor: Yes, caching is supported KV cache persists for the same model family and compatible quant profiles. If you switch to a different family you might lose warm cache. We'll show the matrix where we flag KV cache compatibility per variant.
[02:40] Samir: On quality: can we see evals against our clinical prompt set?
[02:46] Sofia: We can run a small eval in the POC. For the demo here Connor will show our benchmark harness and some public evals, but the console lets you upload a custom prompt set for quality regressions and get metric diffs.
[03:00] [03:00] Connor: (narrating) here's the benchmark detail page p50 and p95 latencies, tokens/sec, memory footprint, and a quality score column for example tasks (summarization F1-ish proxy). You'll also see a 'Compatibility matrix' CSV download button.
[03:20] Alex: Are those quality scores from internal evals or from your customers?
[03:24] Connor: Mostly internal + open benchmark datasets. We surface the test corpora. For clinical we often run medNLP-style evals; in a POC we'll run against your labeled prompts.
[03:34] Jordan: Security: what about KMS/HSM integration and audit logs? We need customer-managed keys and full request audit.
[03:41] Sofia: Redwood Private supports KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-HSM options) and audit logs. We'll attach our SOC 2 and encryption docs.
[03:52] [04:00] Priya: If we go Dedicated vs Private, what's the migration path? We may start hosted then move to VPC.
[04:07] Connor: The API is identical across modes. The Console allows you to pin model versions and rollout policies. We support canary deploys and automatic fallback to compatible smaller variants if capacity is constrained that's your reliability lever.
[04:20] Samir: Can the catalog filter show models that are VM/hardware-compatible with our on-prem A100s?
[04:26] Connor: Yes, filter by hardware compatibility. The matrix flags whether a model's optimized kernels are validated on A100. For older drivers there's a notes column sometimes int8 perf needs newer drivers.
[04:38] [05:00] Connor: Quick demo of Optimize suggestions: the Console recommends batch sizes, quantization profiles, and cache TTLs based on your traffic shape. For example, it suggests int8-4 for open-llm-med-13b to hit your latency target at 1.5k tokens. It's a heuristic but we can run exact bench after we get your prompts.
[05:20] Priya: Interesting how do you measure hallucination risk when quantizing? We can't degrade clinical accuracy.
[05:28] Connor: We always recommend running a quality regression suite on your prompts post-quant. The Console's eval runner highlights differences in key metrics; if we see regression above a threshold we recommend keeping fp16 or using selective quantization.
[05:40] Alex: About throughput: our busiest endpoint will get bursts of 200 qps, typical 30 qps. Will Redwood batching help without impacting p95?
[05:48] Connor: Continuous batching and dynamic batching are tuned to prioritize latency-SLO traffic over throughput busy queues. You can configure per-route latency SLOs in the Console and the router will favor lower-latency paths.
[06:00] [06:00] Jordan: Any mention of competitors do you compare to OpenAI or Bedrock in the console?
[06:05] Sofia: We sometimes show normalized comparisons; customers often benchmark against OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock. We'll include an example bench sheet.
[06:12] Priya: For the POC infra, will you need us to open ports for dedicated testing or can we run remote bench with host-only?
[06:18] Connor: Two options: we can run remote synthetic bench on hosted instances, or for real-data POC we recommend a short-lived VPC peering or a SSH tunnel into your test infra. We'll coordinate with your security team.
[06:30] [07:00] Connor: (scrolling) here's the CSV from the compatibility matrix. Note the columns: model_name, variant, fp_precision, supported_kernels, validated_hardware, kv_cache_compat, notes.
[07:12] Alex: Good to see kv_cache_compat column.
[07:16] Samir: One more can the console detect license terms for open models? We need to avoid restricted licenses.
[07:22] Sofia: Yes, we annotate license metadata in the catalog (MIT, Apache-2.0, etc.) and flag models with non-commercial or incompatible licenses.
[07:30] [08:00] Priya: Okay, can we talk about fallback policies if a big model is unavailable we want automatic fallback but not to a lower-accuracy family unless a human approves.
[08:09] Connor: You can configure fallback rules by family and by route: strict fallbacks only to previously approved variants or a 'degraded but acceptable' list. We also support alerting if fallback rates exceed threshold.
[08:20] Jordan: About logs do you store customer prompts? We need to ensure PHI isn't persisted in hosted mode.
[08:27] Sofia: By default hosted API may temporarily cache for performance but we have data retention controls and can disable persistence. For PHI we recommend Private with customer-managed keys and no persistence. We'll include retention controls in the security doc.
[08:40] [09:00] Priya: Excellent. From our side, success criteria: equal-or-better summary quality vs current RAG pipeline, <200ms p95, and < $0.015 per summary.
[09:10] Sofia: Noted. We'll aim to identify 2-3 model+quant profiles that meet those constraints in the POC.
[09:18] Connor: For the POC we typically run batch bench across 4 variants: base fp16, int8, int4, and a distilled smaller family. We'll measure p95, tokens/sec, and a label-based quality metric on your prompts.
[09:30] [10:00] (short cross talk)
[10:10] Samir: Any known gotchas with A100 drivers and int4?
[10:14] Connor: Some driver versions can cause perf cliffs for int4 kernels. The matrix notes driver minimums; we'll recommend versions or use our dedicated validated images if you prefer.
[10:26] Priya: Cool. Let's lock next steps.
[10:30] Sofia: Recap: we'll send the model catalog deck and console recording, Connor will share bench CSV and compatibility matrix, Midtown will provide prompts and security requirements, then we schedule POC bench. I'll follow up with calendar invites.
[10:43] Jordan: I'll get the security questionnaire back to you by Friday.
[10:46] Alex: I'll pull together traffic patterns and sample prompts.
[10:50] Sofia: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[10:55] Priya: Thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicate' -> 'Redwood Dedicated'), timestamps approximate. References: model catalog doc (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/model-catalog), bench spreadsheet (will be shared), compatibility CSV available in Console.
